newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Sadia says in talks to buy U.S. soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Sadia says in talks to buy U.S. soybeans.

text.p: Brazilian processor Sadia is still in preliminary talks to purchase U.S. soybeans but plans to start buying as soon as Brazilian soybean exports top the eight million tonne mark, a source at the company said.
"We haven't bought anything yet, we are studying (the options)," said the company official, responding to market talk that Sadia had already bought U.S. beans.
"We have already had some indications from firms such as Cargill, Continental and Dreyfus," he said.

Last week, Ceval Alimentos said it had bought 150,000 tonnes U.S. soybeans for October, November and December shipment. Traders reported talk that several other Brazilian firms, including Sadia, were also in the market for U.S. product.
"If Brazil exports more than eight million tonnes, we are going to have to negotiate imports," said the Sadia official.
There were no reliable export figures but Brazil was already "very close" to hitting the eight million tonne mark, he said.
"Due to the lack of reliable figures we are going to have to wait a little. Only after July will we have a better idea," he added.

Brazilian soybean exports are forecast to hit 8.5 million tonnes in the 1997/98 marketing year (February to January) compared to 3.65 million tonnes in 1996/97, according to the Brazilian Vegetable Oils Industries Association (Abiove).
When Sadia starts importing, it will ship soybeans from the U.S. Gulf to its factory at Paranagua port, said the official.
"FOB cargoes from the Gulf should start to arrive from October and CIF cargoes from the second half of October, beginning of November," he said.

For logistical reasons, the company was more likely to import soymeal from Paraguay, a traditional supplier of soybeans and soyproducts to Brazil, the official said. Sadia would prefer U.S. to Argentine beans, he added.
"Argentina has not been very competitive so far. U.S. industries are being more aggressive," he said.
